definitions.explanation: A student who transfers into a school, university, or program partway through, typically entering at a year other than the first. Common in the Japanese university system where students from junior colleges or technical colleges transfer into the third year of a four-year university.

examples.japanese: {編入生|へんにゅうせい}として{大学|だいがく}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: To enter a university as a transfer student.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{編入生|へんにゅうせい}が{十名|じゅうめい}{入学|にゅうがく}した。
examples.english: Ten transfer students enrolled this year.

examples.japanese: {編入生|へんにゅうせい}は{三年次|さんねんじ}から{授業|じゅぎょう}に{参加|さんか}するため、{友達|ともだち}を{作|つく}るのが{難|むずか}しいこともある。
examples.english: Since transfer students join classes from the third year, it can sometimes be difficult to make friends.

notes:
Composed of {編入|へんにゅう} (transfer, incorporation) and {生|せい} (student). Specifically refers to students who enter a school or university at a point other than the normal starting point.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {編入生|へんにゅうせい}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる: to accept transfer students
- {編入生|へんにゅうせい}{向|む}けの{説明会|せつめいかい}: orientation for transfer students
- {三年次|さんねんじ}{編入生|へんにゅうせい}: third-year transfer student

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {編入|へんにゅう} is a well-established pathway in higher education. Students from {短期大学|たんきだいがく} (junior colleges) or {高等専門学校|こうとうせんもんがっこう} (technical colleges) often transfer into the third year of a four-year university. This requires passing a separate {編入試験|へんにゅうしけん} (transfer examination).

RELATED WORDS:
- {転校生|てんこうせい}: transfer student (between schools of the same level) — typically used for elementary through high school
- {留学生|りゅうがくせい}: international student — a student studying abroad
- {編入試験|へんにゅうしけん}: transfer examination — the entrance exam for transfer admission
